Overview of activities, risk factors 2.6 Risk Factors DANONE UNIVERSAL REGISTRATION DOCUMENT 2020 24 DESCRIPTION DESCRIPTION RISK MANAGEMENT MEASURES RISK MANAGEMENT MEASURES high Rapid evolution of consumer preferences Faced with the rapid evolution of consumer preferences and habits, Danone must constantly innovate and adapt its product range and its entire supply chain. The diversification of tastes and eating habits, as well as consumers' increased awareness of health, social and environmental issues, influence their purchases. The major trends in the food sector are notably: · the nutritional quality of products, including the presence or absence of certain ingredients (e.g., sugar, protein, additives);
packaging circularity (see packaging risk above); · sustainable sourcing of ingredients with a proven environmental or social impact; · product origin and company transparency around the brand (strong local trend). The Covid-19 health crisis has generally accelerated several of these consumption trends, reinforcing the importance of health (health benefits, for example immunity, as well as naturalness compared to ultra-processed products), locality, transparency and actors in the food chain. Authorities and distributors are also increasingly attentive to consumer concerns regarding social, environmental and health matters, mainly with regard to (i) health benefits, (ii) local origin, (iii) labeling on nutritional quality and/or the environmental footprint of products and their packaging, as well as (iv) food waste.
If Danone fails (i) to anticipate quickly enough the evolving consumer preferences in terms of taste, eating habits, and environmental expectations, (ii) to identify these consumption trends, (iii) to translate them into appropriate product offerings, and/or (iv) to keep up with the evolution of these preferences, the demand for Danone products and its sales could be affected, the Company could suffer losses, and its operations, results, and reputation could be negatively impacted.
The Company's One Planet. One Health action framework and the Danone 2030 Objectives of the long-term strategy have been defined to better address the challenges of the ongoing food revolution and to better seize the opportunities arising from it.
Danone has also developed a vast product portfolio focused on healthy categories. Its research and innovation expertise allows it to develop a wide range of products and thus meet different diets, nutritional needs, and situations. As an illustration, with the acquisition of WhiteWave in 2017, the Company diversified its portfolio to include organic and plant-based protein products in response to the rapid evolution of certain consumption trends, such as flexitarianism. In 2020, plant-based products represented over 2.2 billion euros in revenue, or nearly 10% of the Company's revenue and just under 20% of the total revenue of the Fresh Dairy Products and Plant-based segment.
Furthermore, Danone strives to encourage continuous dialogue with its consumers by adapting to their new expectations and behaviors, and by demonstrating greater transparency, particularly through digital communication tools regarding its societal and environmental commitments (such as the circular economy of packaging and regenerative agriculture).
Through its Manifesto Brand model and its ambition to obtain B Corp(TM) certification, Danone also aims to develop committed brands and adhere to the strictest social and environmental standards.
Finally, Danone announced in November 2020 the launch of a study for the implementation of a new organization, through a plan called Local First, which aims to increase its local agility to better understand the rapid evolution of consumer preferences and seize new growth opportunities. For more information on product content and environmental footprint, water resources, plastic packaging and sustainable sourcing, see paragraphs 5.3 Preserving the planet and renewing its resources and 5.5 Promoting sustainable and inclusive growth with suppliers.
2 Overview of activities, risk factors 2.6 Risk factors DANONE UNIVERSAL REGISTRATION DOCUMENT 2020 25 DESCRIPTION DESCRIPTION RISK MANAGEMENT MEASURES RISK MANAGEMENT MEASURES moderate Transformation of distribution channels Several structural factors contribute to the rapid evolution of distribution: · consumers' demand for immediacy; · their expectations for healthier food; · their growing need for specific products and services. As a result, there is increasing segmentation of distribution channels, some of which are growing faster (such as hard discount, convenience stores, e-business, and Cash & Carry) and capturing all market growth, while large retailers (such as hypermarkets) continue to decline. The Covid-19 pandemic has accelerated these trends as consumers seek safer options and may be restricted in their travel. For example, online sales of food and beverages in some of Danone's key markets saw double-digit growth in 2020, particularly in France (+21%), the United States (+44%), and China (+55%) (Source: Edge).
The Covid-19 pandemic also creates great uncertainty regarding its effects on out-of-home and proximity channels, which it exposes to additional risks of administrative or voluntary closures, as well as limitations on cross-border trade, as Danone experienced in 2020. The Waters division's activity was severely affected, with a 17% drop in its sales on a like-for-like basis in 2020.
Danone's customers (distributors) are directly affected by the pandemic's effects and associated risks, and are refocusing, in particular, on reduced product reference ranges for many reasons, such as (i) supply chain agility during periods of demand volatility, (ii) the pursuit of profitability, as well as (iii) the integration of the trend towards smaller formats. In this context, if Danone is unable to anticipate market changes and adapt its sales strategy, its market approach strategy, its digital and e-commerce capabilities, and its supply chain and execution model, it could experience:
a slowdown in its growth due to market share losses and inadequate innovation; · pressure on its operating margin; with negative consequences on its financial situation. To adapt to evolving distribution channels, Danone is implementing numerous initiatives, notably: · adapting its commercial strategy to growing channels (route-to-market/execution); · establishing dedicated teams and projects to strengthen its presence in the e-business sector; · identifying partnerships in appropriate regions and channels; · revising the supply model from an economy of scale model to an economy of product ranges model; · using co-packing where appropriate. Furthermore, Danone has dedicated a portion of its accelerated investment plan of approximately 2 billion euros, announced in February 2020, to building an agile, digital, and fully connected value chain, strengthening execution, and better meeting consumer needs, anywhere and at any time (see paragraph 2.2 Strategic Axes).
In addition, Danone has initiated the reorganization of its global portfolio of brands and references, in order to simplify it and promote profitable growth.

But over time, we will have a dramatically lower level of customer deposits, which are recognized on the balance sheet. We expect to finish our global rollout of delayed payment capture in Q4 of this fiscal year.

Clearly, print is in a secular decline over multiple years. I know HP recognises that. They've been trying to invest in certain areas where there are potential areas for growth, while, at the same time, protecting some of their legacy businesses against either print suppression or third-party consumables vendors from developing countries. I think they continue to be disappointed in the commercial/enterprise reduction in print volume due to the pandemic. No one saw that coming. They were facing a lot of headwinds before that happened. As you know, the print part of the business is absolutely the most profitable part of the business, while the personal systems is the higher revenue but with much lower margins. They were somewhat fortunate to receive a benefit of the work at home movement and therefore to benefit from the purchasing of new personal systems and monitors for home offices. The custom in the pharmaceutical industry is generally to grant customers a shelf stock adjustment based on the customers' existing inventory contemporaneously with decreases in the market price of the related product. The most significant of these relate to products for which an exclusive or semi-exclusive period exists. Provisions for price reductions depend on future events, including price competition, new competitive launches and the level of customer inventories at the time of the price decline. Teva regularly monitors the competitive factors that influence the pricing of its products and customer inventory levels and adjust these estimates where appropriate.
Returns
Returns primarily relate to customer returns of expired products which, the customer has the right to return up to one year following the expiration date. Such returned products are destroyed and credits and/or refunds are issued to the customer for the value of the returns. Accordingly, no returned assets are recoded in connection with those products. The returns provision is estimated by applying a historical return rate to the amounts of revenue estimated to be subject to returns. Revenue subject to returns is estimated based on the lag time from time of sale to date of return. The estimated lag time is developed by analyzing historical experience. Additionally, The Company considers specific factors, such as estimated levels of inventory in the distribution channel, product dating and expiration, size and maturity of launch, entrance of new competitors, changes in formularies or packaging and any changes to customer terms, for determining the overall expected levels of returns.

headline: One way to reform the Chapter 11 bankruptcy process
chunk_text:
The Hertz Corporation must look at AMC Entertainment and wonder what might have been. Hertz, pummelled in the early weeks of pandemic, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in May last year. However, in the weeks afterwards, its shares surprisingly rallied around 800 per cent amid a surge of buying by retail traders on the Robinhood app.
The company quickly received court approval to take advantage of its quirky trading to sell new shares where proceeds would partially fund its restructuring. Ultimately it proved all for naught as the US Securities and Exchange Commission declined to sign off on the risk disclosures made to investors. Hertz would never sell its shares, instead moving on to an expensive senior loan.
Meanwhile, the cinema chain AMC has arguably been hammered at least as much by stay-at-home orders as Hertz. In its most recent quarter, AMC's recently stated that its US attendance is down 91 per cent year-over-year. headline: Junk-rated companies enjoy record-low US borrowing costs
chunk_text:
The Federal Reserve's historic monetary policy intervention during the coronavirus crisis and its pledge to underpin markets has given investors the confidence to lend to higher-risk borrowers. Falling yields on higher-rated and sovereign debt have also pushed them to stretch down the credit rating spectrum in search of higher returns.
"Everyone has the same view and there is so much money chasing this rally," said Philipson. "There is such a reach for yield."
Centene, MDC and T-Mobile all sit at the higher end of the junk-rated ladder, with ratings around double B, just one tier below the triple B cut-off to be considered investment-grade.
Nonetheless, the low borrowing costs are stark, less than the US government - widely considered to be one of the world's safest borrowers - was paying on its 10-year debt at the start of 2019.

In 2020, our direct-to-consumer model and synergies from our vertical integration as the exclusive designer, manufacturer, marketer, retailer and servicer of Sleep Number® beds enabled us to deliver a better, faster, simpler, safer and more engaging experience for our customers and our team members. headline: Webull vs Robinhood - Competitive Strategies & Profitability (Conducted in Mandarin)

I think there are two aspects. The first is the stability of the system, which is from the technical point of view. The stock market is intrinsically volatile. Large fluctuations may occur due to some news or events.
Besides, transaction volume will increase when the stock market is opening and will decline when it comes to lunch time. The fluctuations in the same day will bring burdens or difficulties to the system. If the server provision is not enough, the company is able to serve customers well when the transaction volume is not high. However, once large fluctuations occur, such as the greatly increasing transaction volume when the stock market is opening, the system may break down. Even if the system doesn't break down, there will be high latency, which will result in poor customer experience.
I used to work at Robinhood and have used the products of Futu Securities and Tiger Brokers. I think Robinhood performs the best among these companies. The customer size of Futu Securities, Tiger Brokers and Webull is smaller than that of Robinhood. I don't think their systems have encountered the same challenge as Robinhood has in the past year. They haven't seen such demand, so they won't spend too much energy to build their system as complete as possible and they just start from the simplest systems. Therefore, I think they should make more efforts to catch up with Robinhood in this regard.
The second is the function and feature of the system. The biggest difference between Robinhood and Futu Securities and Webull is that Robinhood can carry out independent clearing and it owns the whole technology stack from the exchanges to customers, while Futu Securities and Webull use third-party clearing software to realise this function.

headline: Emerging markets at risk of cyberattacks as COVID-19 drives digital growth
chunk_text:
Shortly after this, Bhinneka, one of Tokopedia's e-commerce rivals, announced it had also been the victim of a cyberattack, with hackers gaining access to 1.2 million accounts.
In a sign of the how widespread cyberthreats are in the region, a report from data security company Trend Micro found that 80 percent of Asia-Pacific organisations had suffered a cyberattack last year.
Meanwhile, in the Middle East, the UAE experienced a 250 percent increase in attacks, according to government officials, with financial services firms and hospitals among the most targeted.
The scale and high-profile nature of many cyberattacks, combined with an increased reliance on digital technology, has ultimately led to a rise in cybersecurity awareness.
In fact, PwC's Global Digital Trust Insights 2021, a survey of more than 3000 business, technology and security executives based around the world, found that 96 percent of respondents had changed or were intending to change their cybersecurity strategies due to COVID-19.
In a sign of growing concern, 55 percent said they would increase their cyber budget moving forward, while 51 percent said they would add dedicated, full-time cybersecurity staff, even though nearly two-thirds thought revenues were set to decline. Meanwhile, one half of respondents said that cybersecurity or privacy measures were now incorporated into every business decision or plan, up from 25 percent just a year ago.
On top of business-level solutions, a number of governments have also sought to bolster online security. In light of the sharp rise in attacks in Indonesia, the government worked on a Personal Data Protection Bill in 2020.
